items.q: What is Every Night, Just Me?
items.a: A postpartum night-coordination system: a written roster both adults follow, three contract templates, a sleep banker that makes invisible exhaustion tradeable, and the scripts to get a resistant partner on board - so the mother gets one protected 4-5 hour sleep opportunity most nights.

A breastfeeding or formula-feeding mother, 0-12 weeks postpartum, doing 100% of night care while her partner sleeps through or is minimally involved - or a mother with no partner in the home who can build a support-web roster.

6 components: The Argument That Ends the War (read); Tonight's Shift Chart + Contract Templates (do); Which Night Model Fits Us? (decide); the 14-Day Night Tracker (track); Seven Script Cards (communicate); and the Bad Night Protocol + safety gate (rescue).
No. Educational content - not medical, clinical, or mental-health advice. This coordinates night-care between adults; it never diagnoses or treats any condition and never replaces professional care.
items.evidence_label: Educational content informed by relationship research, postpartum guidance, and lived experience. It is not a substitute for medical, clinical, or mental-health assessment.

items.q: I'm breastfeeding - can this even work for me?
items.a: Yes. The contract does not pretend you can be off duty all night. It schedules a milk hand-off (a pumped bottle, or your partner brings the baby to feed and returns her to the crib) so your protected block is physically real.

Because the recurring failure is not goodwill, it is the absence of a system: with no written default, the night is renegotiated every time, and the default becomes she owns all of it. A written roster, a named partner shift, and a sleep banker replace an endless negotiation with an agreed rule.
